newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Rivlin - economy growing as fast as it can.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Rivlin - economy growing as fast as it can.

text.p: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alice Rivlin said Friday that the U.S. economy is growing about as fast as it can and is very close to full employment.
"What is true now is the economy is apparently growing about as fast as it can," Rivlin said at a Society of Government Economists conference.
Rivlin said the labor force is growing at about one percent a year and productivity is also growing at about that same pace.
"We're fully employed or certainly very close to full employment," Rivlin said.
The Fed does not want inflation to accelerate, she added.
"The Federal Reserve, as everybody else, is watching the economy very carefully, because the thing we don't want to have happen is for inflation to begin to accelerate," she said.
While most economists thought inflation would begin to accelerate at unemployment rates as low as 5.2 percent, "we haven't seen that yet," Rivlin said.

"It's not clear whether we haven't seen it yet, or whether we are in a new situation" in which for various reasons the United States can sustain unemployment rates at current levels without inflation, she said.
